mainTopic: How to measure a sale or gift by its exact wording: boundary language in a field sale, giving someone a 'portion' (חֵלֶק) of property, and a לוי who keeps the מעשר ראשון when selling his field.
overview: The amud opens by rejecting an earlier reading of the boundary phrases in a field sale. רב יימר בר שלמיה reports from אביי that the deciding factor is whether the seller said 'these are its boundaries.' If he did, the buyer gets half the field; if not, only nine קבין. The גמרא then asks how much someone gets when the giver says 'give so-and-so a portion (חלק) of my property.' רבינא בר קיסי answers with a ברייתא in which סומכוס rules that a plain 'portion' of a cistern is at least a quarter. Next, a ברייתא teaches that a לוי who sells a field can keep the מעשר ראשון for himself, or for himself and his sons. If he limited it to 'as long as the field is in your hand,' the right ends once the buyer sells it. The גמרא asks how this works, since nobody can transfer something that does not exist yet. It answers that the seller held back the part of the land that produces the tithe, and ריש לקיש learns from this that a seller can keep the upper story of a house he sells.

steps.title: אביי's rule: the words 'these are its boundaries' decide
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the earlier view. רב יימר בר שלמיה reports that אביי told him: with either boundary phrase, if the seller said 'these are its boundaries' the buyer gets half, and if not, he gets only nine קבין.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is not correct. רב יימר בר שלמיה said that אביי explained it to him this way. It does not matter whether the seller wrote 'the boundary is the land that halves it' or 'the boundary is the land that is cut off from it.' If he told the buyer 'these are its boundaries,' the buyer gets half. If he did not say that, the buyer gets only a field of nine קבין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the previous explanation. It replaces it with אביי's rule, as reported by רב יימר בר שלמיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier view tied the result to which boundary phrase the seller used. אביי says the two phrases make no difference. What matters is whether the seller added 'these are its boundaries'; without that, the buyer gets only the smaller amount of nine קבין.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is not so: the גמרא is rejecting what came before.
Nine קבין: a field big enough to plant nine קבין of seed.

steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, the exact boundary phrase does not decide the size. Only the words 'these are its boundaries' turn the sale into half the field.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the two phrases (פלגא and פסיקא) give different results. The whole point of this step is that they are treated the same.

phrases.english: But it is not so,
as Rav Yeimar bar Shelemya said:
To me it was explained by Abaye:
Whether he wrote 'the boundary is the land from which it is halved,'
or he wrote 'the boundary is the land from which it is cut off' —
if he said to him 'these are its boundaries,' he gets half;

phrases.aramaic: לָא אֲמַר לֵיהּ: ״אִלֵּין מִצְרָנַהָא״ – תִּשְׁעָה קַבִּין.
phrases.english: if he did not say to him 'these are its boundaries,' he gets nine kav.
phrases.notes: This means a field big enough to plant nine קבין of seed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא הִיא, דְּאָמַר רַב יֵימַר בַּר שֶׁלֶמְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the explanation of the boundary phrases given just before this point.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The earlier view that the result depends on which boundary phrase the seller used.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The deciding factor is whether the seller said 'these are its boundaries,' not which of the two phrases he used.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If he said 'these are its boundaries,' the buyer gets half. If not, the buyer gets nine קבין.

steps.title: What does 'give so-and-so a portion' mean?
steps.stepSummary: It is obvious that 'so-and-so should share in my property' means half. The גמרא asks what 'give so-and-so a portion of my property' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious that if a person said 'so-and-so should share in my property,' he gets half. But if he said 'give so-and-so a portion of my property,' how much does he get?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new, related question about how to measure a gift based on its wording. This sets up the next step, where an answer is offered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'share' (יחלוק) suggests splitting the property into two, so it plainly means half. The word 'portion' (חלק) gives no amount, so the גמרא asks how big that portion should be.

phrases.english: It is obvious that if he said:
'So-and-so should share in my property,' he gets half.
If he said 'Give a portion to so-and-so of my property,' what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from boundary wording in a sale to the wording of a gift. Both ask how much someone gets based on the words used.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How large a share someone receives when the giver says 'give him a portion' without naming an amount.

steps.title: סומכוס on a 'portion' of a cistern
steps.stepSummary: רבינא בר קיסי brings a ברייתא. There, סומכוס rules that 'a portion of a cistern' means at least a quarter, with smaller fractions when a container is named.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא בר קיסי said: Come and hear a source. A ברייתא teaches about someone who says 'give so-and-so a portion of the cistern.' סומכוס says he gets no less than a quarter. If he said 'for a barrel,' he gets no less than an eighth. If he said 'for a pot,' he gets no less than a twelfth. If he said 'for a cup,' he gets no less than a sixteenth.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא בר קיסי answers the question by bringing a ברייתא about a 'portion' of a cistern.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, a plain 'portion' with no container named is a quarter. Each smaller container named lowers the share. So the ברייתא suggests that a plain 'portion' of property should also mean a quarter.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: a proof is being brought.
A small vessel, like a cup or jug.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבִינָא בַּר קִיסִי, תָּא שְׁמַע:
phrases.english: Ravina bar Kisi said: Come and hear:
As it is taught in a baraita: One who says:
'Give a portion to so-and-so of the cistern' —
Sumakhos says: not less than a quarter.
'For a barrel' — not less than an eighth.
'For a pot' — not less than a twelfth.
'For a cup' — not less than a sixteenth.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבִינָא בַּר קִיסִי, תָּא שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a source to answer the question about 'give him a portion.'
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with סומכוס's ruling that a plain portion of a cistern is at least a quarter.
steps.whatToRemember: According to סומכוס, an unspecified 'portion' means at least a quarter.

steps.title: A לוי sells a field but keeps the מעשר ראשון
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a לוי who sells a field on condition that the מעשר ראשון stays his keeps that tithe. If he said 'for me and my sons,' his sons receive it after he dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: A לוי sold a field to a ישראל and said 'on condition that the מעשר ראשון is mine.' Then the מעשר ראשון is his. If he said 'to me and to my sons,' and he dies, the buyer gives it to his sons.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about a seller who keeps something for himself when he sells. Here it is the right to the מעשר ראשון from the field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a ישראל can give his מעשר ראשון to any לוי he chooses. Here the seller made a condition that it must go to him. If he named only himself, the condition covers him; if he added 'my sons,' it continues to his sons after his death.

keyTerms.meaning: The רבנן taught: introduces a ברייתא.
A לוי, a member of the tribe of לוי.
The first tithe, which is given to a לוי.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
A Levite who sold a field to an Israelite,
and said to him:
'On condition that the first tithe is mine' —
the first tithe is his.
And if he said: 'To me and to my sons' —
if he dies, he must give it to his sons.
phrases.notes: 'He' who gives is the buyer: he now hands the tithe to the לוי's sons.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: בֶּן לֵוִי שֶׁמָּכַר שָׂדֶה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: a seller who keeps a right for himself in a sale.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A לוי who sells a field on condition that the מעשר ראשון is his gets it. If he included his sons, they get it after he dies.

steps.title: A condition that lasts only while the buyer holds the field
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes. If the לוי said the tithe stays his 'as long as this field is in your hand,' then once the buyer sells the field, the right ends. It does not come back even if the buyer later buys the field back.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he said to him, 'as long as this field is in your possession,' and the buyer sold it and later bought it back, the seller has no claim on him at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from the last step adds one final case: a condition that is tied to the buyer holding the field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the לוי's right to the מעשר ראשון depends on the field staying with the buyer. Once the field leaves the buyer's hands, even for a short time, the condition is finished for good. Buying it back later does not bring the right back.

keyTerms.meaning: in your hand, meaning in your possession
he went back and bought it again
he has no claim on him at all

phrases.english: But if he said to him:
phrases.notes: The seller, the לוי, is speaking to the buyer.

phrases.english: "As long as this field is in your possession" –
and the buyer sold it and then bought it back,
the seller has no claim on him at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם אָמַר לוֹ: כׇּל זְמַן שֶׁהַשָּׂדֶה זוֹ בְּיָדְךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא from step 4 with a condition that has a time limit.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A condition limited to 'as long as the field is in your hand' ends for good once the buyer sells the field.

steps.title: How can he keep produce that does not exist yet?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא: how can the seller keep the tithe of future crops? A person cannot transfer something that has not come into the world yet.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why? A person cannot transfer ownership of something that has not yet come into the world!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the basic ruling of the ברייתא using a well-known rule of acquiring.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The crops that will be tithed have not grown yet. By the rule of דבר שלא בא לעולם, nobody can transfer or hold on to rights in something that does not exist yet. So it seems the seller's condition should not work at all.

keyTerms.meaning: why?, a word that often opens a challenge
something that has not yet come into the world, meaning it does not exist yet

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether the condition is fair. It is whether ownership of things that do not exist yet can be held or transferred at all.

phrases.english: Why?
A person cannot transfer ownership
of something that has not yet come into the world!
phrases.notes: The crops that will be tithed haven't grown yet, so right now they don't exist.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמַּאי? אֵין אָדָם מַקְנֶה דָּבָר שֶׁלֹּא בָּא לָעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of the ברייתא quoted in steps 4 and 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that the seller keeps the מעשר ראשון of future crops.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Future crops do not exist yet, and you cannot transfer or keep rights in something that does not exist yet.

steps.title: He held back the land where the tithe grows
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that by saying 'on condition that the first tithe is mine,' the seller held back for himself the piece of land where the tithe grows. That land already exists.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since he said to him, 'on condition that the first tithe is mine,' he held back for himself the place of the tithe.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by changing what the seller is understood to have kept.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The seller did not keep future crops. He never sold one part of the land itself, the part that will produce the tithe. Land already exists, so the rule of דבר שלא בא לעולם does not apply, and the crops that grow there are simply his.

keyTerms.meaning: he held it back for himself and did not include it in the sale
the place of the tithe, meaning the part of the land that produces it

steps.whatToRemember: Holding back part of what you sell (שיור) works even for future produce. You are keeping part of something that exists now, not taking possession of something new.
steps.whyThisMatters: This idea of holding back is the basis for ריש לקיש's ruling in the next step.

phrases.english: Since he said to him:
"On condition that the first tithe is mine" –
he held back for himself the place of the tithe.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּאָמַר לֵיהּ: עַל מְנָת שֶׁמַּעֲשֵׂר רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁלִּי
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining what was kept: existing land rather than future produce.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The seller is trying to keep crops that do not exist yet, which should not work.
steps.terutzMaskana: The seller held back the part of the land where the tithe grows, which already exists, so the condition works.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: a seller can keep the upper story
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש learns from this ברייתא that someone who sells a house 'on condition that the upper story is mine' really does keep the upper story.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: This teaches that if someone sells a house to another person and says, 'on condition that the upper story is mine,' the upper story is his.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש draws a new ruling about houses from the ברייתא about the field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the words זאת אומרת ('this teaches'), ריש לקיש applies the idea of holding back from step 7 to a house. Just as the seller kept the patch of land for the tithe, a seller can keep the upper story of a house when he sells the rest. The upper story stays his.

keyTerms.meaning: this teaches, a phrase used to learn a new rule from an earlier source
the upper story of a house

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
This is to say,
one who sells a house to another
and says to him:
"On condition that the upper story is mine" –
the upper story is his.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the idea of holding back from step 7 and applies it to selling a house.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who sells a house but keeps the upper story by stating it as a condition keeps the upper story.
